daily.title: AI leaders call for regulations, Trump dismisses 'hoaxes'
daily.summary: AI giants are working to create a standards body amid rising alarms about the dangers of the industry. Meanwhile, Trump has dismissed the warnings, and a divided US Congress has failed to act.

daily.title: Criticism of LGBTQ+ raids in Turkey is growing
daily.summary: Several raids and arrests of LGBTQ+ persons in Turkey have triggered sharp criticism from numerous Turkish organizations — and also from Brussels.

daily.title: High fuel prices challenge the German government
daily.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz wants to provide relief to motorists. But exactly how this is to happen remains unclear.

daily.title: Knobloch: 'It is a very dangerous situation at the moment'
daily.summary: Charlotte Knobloch survived the Holocaust by passing as the daughter of non-Jewish farmers. She recently spoke with DW to express her shock following the AfD victory in Saxony-Anhalt's state election.

daily.title: South Africa now probing deaths of 8 women near Johannesburg
daily.summary: Police have warned women to take extra care in parts of Johannesburg as similarities between at least eight deaths fuel fears that the cases could be connected.

daily.title: Why do authoritarian regimes target the LGBTQ+ community?
daily.summary: A recent crackdown on the LGBTQ+ community in Turkey is symptomatic of a wider rights regression, according to experts. It's worse under authoritarian regimes, but why is it such a popular policy for these states?

daily.title: Russia: Trump's Ukraine ceasefire proposal is 'good idea'
daily.summary: The Kremlin has hailed an "energy ceasefire" proposed by US President Trump, but has criticized a French initiative to share its nuclear deterrent. Meanwhile, hostilities have continued on the ground and in the air.

daily.title: Ovechkin still backing Putin party in parliamentary vote
daily.summary: Ice hockey legend Alexander Ovechkin has lent Vladimir Putin's party a helping hand in its parliamentary election campaign. That's in keeping with a pattern of support by an athlete who claims not to be political.

daily.title: Spanish scientists find first evidence of Diplodocus dinosaur in Europe
daily.summary: Paleontologists in Spain say they have found the first evidence of the long-necked Diplodocus genus of dinosaur outside of North America. They found bones at the rich La Tejeria fossil site in Teruel in eastern Spain.

daily.title: Saudi Arabia faces hard choices as Houthis gain in Yemen
daily.summary: Saudi Arabia faces growing security and economic problems as it seeks to balance deterrence and diplomacy during its escalating conflict with the Iran-backed Houthis in neighboring Yemen.

daily.title: Why the era of cheap government debt is over
daily.summary: US debt has topped $40 trillion. How risky is the country's growing debt burden. And will investors keep funding Washington's deficits?

daily.title: US allies in Asia alarmed as think tank calls for pullback
daily.summary: Analysts warn that a US withdrawal from the western Pacific, as recently suggested by a think tank, would weaken deterrence and strengthen China's position.

daily.title: 'Woman, Life, Freedom' spirit lives on as Iran war drags on
daily.summary: The 2022 death of Jina Mahsa Amini in police custody triggered a resistance movement in Iran. Four years later, the Iranian regime endures — but so does the legacy of the "Woman, Life, Freedom" protests.

daily.title: Bangladesh court sentences 7 Hasina allies to death
daily.summary: The latest verdict brings to 22 the number of death sentences handed down in cases stemming from the 2024 uprising that ended Sheikh Hasina's 15-year rule.

daily.title: Socialist Left leads far-right AfD ahead of Berlin vote
daily.summary: The results of the Berlin election are as hard to predict as ever. Three parties are vying for first place, including the socialist Left Party and the far-right AfD. But one issue is most important to Berliners.

daily.title: Germany news: Merz to cancel UN trip amid party infighting
daily.summary: Germany's chancellor nixxed his trip over doubts about his leadership after party losses to the AfD in state elections. Meanwhile, Defense Minister Pistorius is in Washington for talks with his US counterpart. Follow DW.

daily.title: SPD governor campaigns as one-woman bulwark against AfD
daily.summary: Manuela Schwesig, of the center-left SPD, has governed the state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, on the Baltic Sea coast, since 2017. Ahead of this weekend's election, she is campaigning against the nationalist AfD.

daily.title: US confirms it has weapons in space
daily.summary: The Space Force justified the weapons deployment by citing the US's two biggest geopolitical rivals: Russia and China. Beijing responded by urging Washington to "stop preparing for war" in outer space.

daily.title: NATO jets shoot down drone over Lithuania
daily.summary: The drone, which is believed to have entered Lithuanian airspace from Belarus, was shot down by an Italian fighter jet in between the cities of Vilnius and Kaunas. There have been no reports of casualties or damage.

daily.title: Russian warship fires flares at Danish helicopter
daily.summary: Denmark has summoned Russia's ambassador over a Baltic Sea encounter that Copenhagen says is part of an increasingly aggressive pattern of Russian behavior.

daily.title: Netherlands: Suspected sabotage disrupts train services
daily.summary: A major outage has hit parts of the Dutch railway system after objects were found placed across lines, authorities say. The company responsible for rail infrastructure says it suspects deliberate wrongdoing.

daily.title: Why AI researchers warn humanity could face extinction
daily.summary: Could artificial intelligence pose an existential threat to humanity? Some leading researchers are warning against an unregulated race toward AI superintelligence.

daily.title: Iran and US: Two countries and the pistachio between them
daily.summary: The pistachios sold across the United States have a surprising history: California's trees trace their roots to Iran. Now, both regions face the same threat — their farmland is sinking as groundwater disappears.

daily.title: Europe launches two climate observation satellites
daily.summary: The European Space Agency has put two satellites into orbit to take a closer look at the impact of climate change. One of them will focus particularly on plant life.

weekly.title: EU seeks Arctic strategy amid growing power rivalry
weekly.summary: Russia's aggression, Trump's threats against Greenland and the race for critical raw materials are pushing the Arctic to the top of Europe's agenda.

weekly.title: Ukraine, Russia set for new round of US-mediated talks
weekly.summary: New trilateral talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US could begin in October, according to Kyiv and Moscow. Few expect a breakthrough, but Ukraine is seeking a partial de-escalation to help it get through the winter.

weekly.title: Trump seeks halt to energy attacks by both Russia, Ukraine
weekly.summary: Donald Trump, under fire for record US diesel prices, claims Russia and Ukraine have agreed to stop striking energy targets. Russia said nothing; Ukraine said "we expect specifics from our partners" on any such move.

weekly.title: Women's Basketball World Cup: Can Germany harness a boom?
weekly.summary: Germany thrilled fans at the Women's Basketball World Cup. But even if this sparked a boom in the women's game, the infrastructure simply isn't ready for it.

weekly.title: Africa's richest man Dangote's IPO out of reach in Nigeria
weekly.summary: Dangote seeks $1.6 billion from investors to finance a $14.3 billion expansion and thus double the oil refinery's capacity. The offer could give millions of Nigerians a stake in the company. But who can truly afford it?

weekly.title: Far-right AfD puts pressure on German aid to Ukraine
weekly.summary: Emboldened by its win in Saxony-Anhalt, the far-right Alternative for Germany wants the government to change its Ukraine and Russia policies. Berlin is staying the course, but support is fading — especially in the east.

weekly.title: The Crusades: How a medieval holy war still shapes politics
weekly.summary: In 1095, the Catholic Church launched the Crusades: wars that left millions dead and whose legacy still shapes political and ideological conflicts.

weekly.title: EU leaders urge unity after Russian strike on train
weekly.summary: Russia's drone attack on a train near the Ukraine-Poland border has triggered EU calls to up support for Kyiv. Allies of Ukraine should show they "are not scared," said the bloc's top diplomat, Kaja Kallas.

weekly.title: Can Iran replace sea trade with land routes?
weekly.summary: Iran is shifting trade toward northern ports and land routes as its southern shipping faces a US blockade. Analysts say the corridors can keep essential goods moving, but cannot replace maritime trade.

weekly.title: In cosmopolitan Berlin, elections still closed to foreigners
weekly.summary: A quarter of Berlin residents will have no say in the German capital's city-state election because they lack citizenship. That's the highest proportion of residents excluded from the election yet, and many are unhappy.

weekly.title: Germany: Merz's CDU comes out on top in Lower Saxony polls
weekly.summary: The Christian Democrats have emerged as the strongest party following local elections in the state of Lower Saxony. The vote was closely watched as an indicator of the strength of the far-right AfD, which came in third.

weekly.title: Germany's Zverev wins US Open in golden year
weekly.summary: Alexander Zverev has won the US Open for the first time, defeating Ben Shelton in the final. It is Zverev's second Grand Slam win of 2026 after a long wait for his first title, but controversy still hangs over him.

weekly.title: Russians on the Goethe-Institut: 'Hostage to politics'
weekly.summary: Canceled language exams, disrupted plans to study in Germany and the disappearance of an important cultural link: DW users shared how the closure of Germany's Goethe-Institut in Russia has affected their lives.

weekly.title: A Romani artist in Hungary reclaims his identity
weekly.summary: Norbert Olah is an artist. He's also Romani. For a long time, he avoided making his ethnic background a theme of his art for fear of being pigeonholed. Then it became his focus.

weekly.title: Why are European banks moving gold out of United States?
weekly.summary: The Netherlands and France have moved their gold out of US vaults. Part of the reason is fears about the reliability of the US, but equally important is the need to keep gold closer to home in the event of a crisis.

weekly.title: Corals as climate archive: Are El Nino events intensifying?
weekly.summary: Records show that El Nino events have been frequent and often extreme over the past few decades. Is this normal? Or is it the result of climate change? Corals can give us a clear indication.

weekly.title: Russia's drone war comes to Moldova and Romania
weekly.summary: Incursions by Russian drones into Moldovan and Romanian airspace are increasingly common. This week the Ukrainian president's plane was stopped from taking off from Chisinau. Observers suspect the attacks are deliberate.

weekly.title: DW exclusive: Zelenskyy offers to meet Putin at G20 in Miami
weekly.summary: In an interview with DW, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said his country was in a strong position to negotiate and offered to meet Vladimir Putin in Miami.

weekly.title: India looks to steer BRICS away from anti-Western turn
weekly.summary: The BRICS summit 2026 takes place in Delhi this weekend. Unlike last year, Putin and Xi are expected to attend. Can India keep the expanded bloc united?

weekly.title: Turks in Germany anxious after AfD wins in Saxony-Anhalt
weekly.summary: The Alternative for Germany party's win in Saxony-Anhalt has alarmed people of Turkish origin in eastern states. Will workers and business owners abandon the increasingly AfD-friendly region for the more welcoming west?

weekly.title: The 'end of an era' as Goethe-Institut in Russia closes
weekly.summary: The Goethe-Institut was one of the last German institutions still operating in Russia. However, following Moscow's decision to close its offices, all employees will have to stop working by September 13.

weekly.title: Magyar vs. Moscow: Hungary toughens stance toward Russia
weekly.summary: Prime Minister Peter Magyar has abruptly ended the era of his predecessor's warm relations with Russia: Hungary has expelled 10 Russian diplomats. The Kremlin is considering halting gas supplies in response.

weekly.title: Germany sets its sights on Russia's shadow fleet
weekly.summary: The German government wants to follow other EU countries and take more decisive action against Russia's shadow fleet, accusing it of helping Moscow evade sanctions and carry out acts of sabotage.

weekly.title: Cyberattack in Berlin: 1.4 million files on the dark web
weekly.summary: Shortly before Berlin's state parliamentary election, the hacker group Rhysida stole data, tried to extort the Berlin Senate and published the data on the dark web after their attempt failed.

weekly.title: How Celine Dion became a pop culture icon across generations
weekly.summary: As the global star kicks off her anticipated Paris residency, here's how Celine Dion managed to gain younger followers while keeping her loyal older fans.

weekly.title: Are electric cars really bad for the environment?
weekly.summary: Some German politicians are calling for a delay to the EU plan to phase out gas-powered vehicles, saying cars must be judged on the entire carbon footprint. But the full picture still says EVs are more climate friendly.

weekly.title: Serbia, the conflicted EU candidate
weekly.summary: On paper, Belgrade has pursued EU membership for years. But accession has long been stalled. The hero's farewell given to war criminal Mladic exposed just how far Serbia has alienated itself from Europe.

weekly.title: How Belarusians still find hope in a silenced country
weekly.summary: The documentary "Letters from the Silenced Country" depicts the ongoing repression under the authoritarian regime. Director Andrei Kutsila talked to DW ahead of the film's Venice premiere.

weekly.title: Why we're still looking for dark matter
weekly.summary: When physicists said they may have spotted evidence of dark matter almost 100 years after it was proposed as a theory, the internet lit up. Here's why we're searching for the thing that holds everything else together.

weekly.title: LIV Golf in financial turmoil: What's next for the sport?
weekly.summary: Six months after Saudi Arabia pulled funding from the breakaway organization, LIV Golf have filed for bankruptcy protection. Several of the world's best players signed on to LIV, so where does that leave golf?

weekly.title: Conspiracy theories can provide answers but not peace
weekly.summary: Twenty-five years after 9/11, conspiracy theories about the terrorist attacks persist. But even as an attempt to make sense of a tragedy, psychologists say the benefit in conspiracy ideation or belief is short-lived.

weekly.title: The billion-euro trade driving Europe's eels to extinction
weekly.summary: Traffickers are making big bucks smuggling millions of critically endangered eels across continents, using suitcases on planes and legal loopholes to deliver them to dinnerplates. Where are the smuggling hotspots?

weekly.title: The Bayeux Tapestry in London: What's behind the hype?
weekly.summary: The exhibition of the Bayeux Tapestry at the British Museum is eagerly anticipated across the UK, as the medieval masterpiece is considered by many to be a symbol of the country's identity.

weekly.title: EU sports commissioner says FIFA is 'damaging to football'
weekly.summary: Speaking to DW, EU Commissioner Glenn Micallef hit out at world football's governing body over its "poor governance."

weekly.title: Putin rejects mobilization rumors, many Russians unconvinced
weekly.summary: Russia’s President Vladimir Putin has dismissed rumors about military mobilization. But many Russians, including many DW users, say they are preparing for the possibility.
